rules.title: Headquarters
rules.text: Heroes and villains keep bases: a cave, the top floors of a tower, an orbital satellite, a moon base. A headquarters is bought with equipment points like any other gear. If it is destroyed, the owner can rebuild it or put the same points into a new base with different features; villains often burn through several lairs.

rules.title: Headquarters traits
rules.text: A headquarters has two traits, Size and Toughness, plus any number of Features. All three cost equipment points.

rules.title: Size
rules.text: Size works like vehicle size and tells how much room the base has. Small (a house) is the free starting size. Each category larger costs 1 point; each category smaller refunds 1 point to spend on the base's other traits. Sizes run Miniscule (a room, -4), Fine (a loft, -3), Diminutive (an apartment, -2), Tiny (a townhouse, -1), Small (a house, 0), Medium (a warehouse, 1), Large (a mansion or cave complex, 2), Huge (a castle, 3), Gargantuan (a skyscraper, 4), Colossal (a city block or private estate, 5), Awesome (a small town or sprawling installation, 6).

rules.title: Toughness
rules.text: Toughness measures the outer structure: walls, roof, hull. A base starts at Toughness 6 for free, and each +2 Toughness costs 1 point (Toughness 10 costs 2, Toughness 20 costs 7).

rules.title: Features
rules.text: Doors, windows, power outlets and utilities come free. Every other feature costs 1 point, and some can be taken several times for a bigger effect (Concealed, Secret and Security System raise their DCs; a second Workshop handles a specialty; Self-Repairing twice rebuilds the base). With GM approval you can invent new features modeled on the book's.

rules.title: Headquarters power level
rules.text: Some features scale with the base's power level. For heroes it is the series power level; for villains it is the owner's effective power level or whatever the GM sets.

rules.title: Cost formula (as DCUGen computes it)
rules.text: Cost = size cost (Small 0, +1 per category up, -1 per category down; Dual Size pays for the interior size) + ceil((Toughness - 6) / 2) + 1 per feature taken (count repeats). A base never costs less than 0, since size refunds can only pay for its own features.

rules.title: Shared headquarters
rules.text: A team usually shares one base and splits its equipment point cost as the members like, usually as evenly as possible. With most bases, no member needs more than one rank of Equipment (5 points) for it, and leftover points can cover team vehicles or gear like commlinks.

rules.title: Alternate headquarters
rules.text: Extra bases (safe houses around the world, back-up lairs) are Alternate Equipment: pay full price for the most expensive and 1 point for each other base of the same or lower cost. A shared team base is the exception: each member pays a share of it and also pays separately for any personal base.

rules.title: Book sample inconsistencies
rules.text: Four of the book's nine sample headquarters (and the hero Batcave sample on DCA 213) do not add up under the book's own cost rules. DCUGen stores the computed cost and keeps the printed number as book_cost with an explanation.

rules.title: House features (DCUGen)
rules.text: Features marked DCUGen come from the user's own headquarters sheet (BaseHQ.xlsx) and follow the book's rule that invented features cost 1 point each with GM approval: Armory, Countermeasures, Dimensional Cells, Food Supply, Game Room, Magic Detection, Motor Pool, Sovereign Territory, Stables, Untraceable, Vault, Shrine.

toughness.text: Starts at Toughness 6 for 0 points; each +2 Toughness costs 1 equipment point.

features.name: Combat Simulator
features.text: A training room whose equipment can simulate any suitable attack effect up to the base's power level, and project illusions to recreate almost any setting. Good for drills and war games, and a classic way to trap intruders, or for intruders to trap the heroes.

features.name: Communications
features.text: Receives and transmits across radio and TV bands, monitors police and emergency channels and links team members. Restricted bands depend on clearance; Technology DC 25 cracks them illegally.

features.name: Computer
features.text: A state-of-the-art system for the whole base: full use of Technology, and it can run routine functions like monitoring channels and defenses. A thinking computer is bought as a minion or sidekick instead.

features.name: Concealed
features.text: The base is hidden (false front, buried, camouflaged): +10 to the DC of checks to find it. Each extra time it is taken adds +5, to a maximum of +30. Separate from Isolated, which makes it hard to reach rather than hard to find.

features.name: Defense System
features.text: Weapon emplacements inside and out. Each can have any attack effect costing up to twice the base's power level, with an attack bonus equal to the power level.

features.name: Deathtraps
features.text: The villain's version of a Defense System: fiendish traps to keep heroes out or dispose of captured ones (auto-guns, flame walls, rooms that flood with water or sand). Not every deathtrap kills; some just capture.

features.name: Dimensional Portal
features.text: A gateway, from a plain door to a humming machine, with two-way travel to another dimension and perhaps several related ones. The GM may require an Expertise or Technology check to work it.

features.name: Dock
features.text: Berths and dry-dock for water vehicles, with an airlock or lock system and access to a nearby waterway. The base must be near water.

features.name: Dual Size
features.text: Bigger inside than out. Pay for the interior size, then set the exterior to any smaller size, no smaller than Miniscule (a phone booth or wardrobe). The GM may allow interiors beyond Awesome, each step doubling, up to pocket universes. Bases with no outside at all use Dimensional Portal, Isolated or Sealed instead.

features.name: Effect
features.text: Any suitable power effect for the base, with GM approval, costing no more than twice the base's power level and within power level limits. It affects the base or its occupants; for both, apply Affects Others or take two features.

features.name: Fire Prevention System
features.text: Automatic detection and suppression: any large open flame triggers a Nullify Fire 5 effect. A computer can be told to ignore certain fires, or the system put on manual.

features.name: Garage
features.text: Houses ground vehicles, with a ramp or elevator, repair facilities and a sliding door.

features.name: Grounds
features.text: Land around the buildings up to three size categories larger than the structure (a base gets one size larger free). Defense and Security Systems cover the grounds too.

features.name: Gym
features.text: Weights, exercise machines, space to train and the usual lockers and showers; can include a pool, even one linked to open water or the dock.

features.name: Hangar
features.text: Houses air and space vehicles, with a launch hatch or runway (maybe via a long tunnel) and maintenance facilities.

features.name: Holding Cells
features.text: Cells for prisoners, fitted either with Nullify devices at the base's power level or with +50% Toughness, as player and GM agree. Taking it twice gives both.

features.name: Infirmary
features.text: Hospital beds and gear for full use of Treatment, handling up to the base's power level in patients at once, including the owners' unusual physiology.

features.name: Isolated
features.text: Far from anywhere: Antarctica, the sea floor, a mountain peak, orbit, the Moon. Life support for the location is included, but not a way to get there.

features.name: Laboratory
features.text: Scientific equipment (and computers if the base has none) for research and for studying odd phenomena, including powers. Some Expertise, Investigation or Technology checks need one or gain a bonus from it.

features.name: Library
features.text: Books, archives and databases for research with Expertise; may be required for, or grant a circumstance bonus to, certain checks.

features.name: Living Space
features.text: Bedrooms, kitchen, dining and common rooms for about as many residents as the base's power level (more at the GM's option).

features.name: Personnel
features.text: A staff sized to the base, run by the GM, who maintain the place and may defend it, but are not minions and do not go on missions. They can be robots, golems, skeletons or trained apes as suits the owner.

features.name: Power System
features.text: Generators of any kind make the base independent of outside power, with back-up power for hours equal to the base's power level.

features.name: Sealed
features.text: Cut off from the outside: no doors or windows, or behind a barrier. Only the owner and invited guests enter, short of effects like Dimensional Travel, Insubstantial, Permeate or Teleport.

features.name: Secret
features.text: Hiding in plain sight (the abandoned house, the closed factory): +10 to the DC to discover it is a base (usually DC 10), +5 per extra time taken, to a maximum of +30.

features.name: Security System
features.text: Locks and alarms: Technology DC 20 to bypass, +5 per extra time taken, to a maximum of DC 40. Can trigger the Defense System.

features.name: Self-Repairing
features.text: The structure heals damage over time like a character recovers. Taken twice, it rebuilds itself within a week even if destroyed, in the nearest suitable place if it must.

features.name: Temporal Limbo
features.text: Time inside runs at half or double the outside rate; each extra time taken doubles the ratio again (quarter or four times, and so on). Good for crash projects or long exiles.

features.name: Workshop
features.text: Tools, benches and supplies for building things: wood, metal, machining. Specialties such as magical inventions need a separate dedicated workshop (take the feature again).

features.name: Teleport
features.text: A teleporter as an Effect feature (usually Teleport with Affects Others) linking the base to the field. Listed this way in the book's Moon-Base and Orbiting Satellite.

features.name: Armory
features.text: Racks of weapons and armor for the base's residents and staff; lets residents re-arm with their own equipment between scenes without a trip elsewhere.

features.name: Countermeasures
features.text: Jammers, scramblers and anti-scrying wards; -2 to remote sensing and electronic surveillance aimed at the base, and helps it stay Untraceable.

features.name: Dimensional Cells
features.text: Holding cells for beings who would slip normal bars: phasers, teleporters and extradimensional entities.

features.name: Food Supply
features.text: Stores, hydroponics or a pantry to keep the residents fed through a long siege or isolation.

features.name: Game Room
features.text: Lounge, games and screens: a place to unwind that helps the team recover from stress and build morale.

features.name: Magic Detection
features.text: Wards and sensors that sense spells cast in or aimed at the base and sound an alarm.

features.name: Motor Pool
features.text: A pool of ordinary cars, vans or boats for residents' everyday use, beyond any vehicles bought with equipment points.

features.name: Sovereign Territory
features.text: The base has embassy or treaty status; local authorities need permission to enter.

features.name: Stables
features.text: Stalls, tack and grooms for mounts and draft animals; the fantasy equivalent of a Garage.

features.name: Untraceable
features.text: Signals, deliveries and power usage cannot be traced back to the base; -8 to Perception and Investigation checks to track them.

features.name: Vault
features.text: A strong room for valuables and dangerous artifacts, Technology DC 40 to crack.

features.name: Shrine
features.text: A consecrated chapel or altar; rituals and Expertise: Magic or religion checks made there gain a +2 circumstance bonus.

premade.name: Abandoned Warehouse
premade.summary: A derelict dockside warehouse quietly converted into a working base.

premade.name: Moon-Base
premade.summary: A sprawling lunar installation linked to Earth by teleporter.
premade.book_cost_note: Book lists 28. Awesome 6 + Toughness 20 (+14 = 7) + 16 features, Security System counted twice for DC 25 = 17, total 30. Even counting Security System once it is 29. The Orbiting Satellite, with the same features minus Workshop and the extra Security rank, is 2 off in the same way.

premade.name: Orbiting Satellite
premade.summary: A watchtower in orbit with a teleporter down to the surface.
premade.book_cost_note: Book lists 25. Colossal 5 + Toughness 20 (7) + 15 features = 27. The Fortress of Solitude sample (Huge, Toughness 20, 15 feature points, 25) shows the book itself pricing Toughness 20 at 7.

premade.name: Sea-Base
premade.summary: A pressurized complex on the sea floor with a submarine dock.
premade.book_cost_note: Book lists 16. Gargantuan 4 + Toughness 14 (4) + 9 features = 17. The Underground Lair (Huge, Toughness 14, 12 features, 19) prices Toughness 14 at 4, so the Sea-Base is 1 short.

premade.name: Skyscraper (5 Floors)
premade.summary: The top five floors of a downtown tower, with a rooftop hangar.

premade.name: Stately Manor
premade.summary: An old-money estate hiding a high-tech headquarters behind the portraits.

premade.name: Underground Lair
premade.summary: A cavern fortress far below the surface, with cells for captured heroes.

premade.name: Urban Fortress
premade.summary: A hardened city building with a training room, cells and a garage.
premade.book_cost_note: Book lists 22. Large 2 + Toughness 12 (3) + 14 features = 19. The Skyscraper (Large, Toughness 10, 13 features) is 17, which the formula reproduces, so the Urban Fortress's 22 is 3 too high.

premade.name: Wizard's Tower
premade.summary: A modest tower on the outside, a castle's worth of halls within.

premade.name: The Cave Beneath the Manor
premade.summary: A cavern under an old family manor, fitted out as a secret base.
premade.book_cost_note: Book lists 20 (and spells Hangar "Hanger"). Huge 3 + Toughness 10 (2) + 14 features = 19; the Stately Manor sample, same size and Toughness with 14 features, is 19.

premade.name: Polar Fortress
premade.summary: A crystal citadel in the Arctic wastes.

premade.name: Ravenhall Manor and the Cave Below
premade.summary: A gothic mansion on the bluffs; behind the grandfather clock, stairs lead down to a cavern of computers, trophies and a turbine-driven car.

premade.name: Vanguard Tower
premade.summary: A gleaming tower in the shape of the team's emblem, with a rooftop hangar and a museum lobby for tourists.

premade.name: Orbital Station
premade.crew: A world-class team on rotating monitor duty
premade.summary: A ring station 22,000 miles up that watches the whole planet and beams heroes wherever they are needed.

premade.name: Abyssal Station
premade.summary: Linked domes on the edge of an ocean trench, lit by bioluminescent gardens.

premade.name: Selene Outpost
premade.summary: A compact moon base buried under regolith in a crater's permanent shadow.

premade.name: Caldera Keep
premade.summary: A volcano lair with a retractable crater lid, a lava moat and a monorail through the magma chamber.

premade.name: Site Nine Bunker
premade.summary: A government black site under a decommissioned missile silo, where captured superhumans are studied.

premade.name: Sanctum of the Ninefold Door
premade.crew: A sorcerer supreme, an apprentice, a few spirits
premade.summary: A narrow brownstone whose nine doors open onto halls, gardens and other worlds.

premade.name: The Interstitial Library

features.name: Temporal Limbo
features.detail: time runs twice as fast inside

premade.summary: A pocket-dimension library reached through any library door at midnight; its stacks hold every book never written.

premade.name: Street Safe House
premade.summary: A walk-up apartment above a laundromat with a police scanner, a cot and a med kit.

premade.name: Hidden Dojo
premade.crew: A martial arts master and students
premade.summary: Behind a tea shop, a training hall of paper screens, practice dummies and ancient scrolls.

premade.name: Abandoned Subway Lair
premade.crew: A vigilante crew or a gang
premade.summary: A sealed-off station from 1904, its tiled platforms turned into workshops and a garage on the old tracks.

premade.name: Skycarrier Bastion
premade.summary: A flying aircraft carrier held aloft by giant rotors; a mobile headquarters that can be anywhere in a day.

premade.name: Meridian Station
premade.summary: A spinning wheel station at a jump point, part port, part embassy, part frontier town.

premade.name: Ironrock Asteroid Fortress
premade.summary: A hollowed nickel-iron asteroid bristling with guns, drifting in a debris field that hides it.

premade.name: Alien Mothership Interior
premade.summary: Organic corridors, specimen labs and abduction bays inside a city-sized ship.

premade.name: Harbor Lighthouse
premade.summary: A working lighthouse whose keeper's cottage hides a boat dock in the sea cave below.

premade.name: Penthouse Command Loft
premade.summary: A glass-walled loft whose coffee table opens into a command console.

premade.name: Corporate Research Campus
premade.summary: A landscaped tech campus where a hero's company builds tomorrow, and a villain's builds weapons.

premade.name: Polar Citadel
premade.summary: A fortress of ice crystals at the top of the world, keeping the relics of a dead planet.

premade.name: Sewer Warren
premade.summary: Storm drains and forgotten cisterns turned into a damp, sprawling hideout.

premade.name: Midway of Mayhem
premade.crew: A clown prince of crime and his troupe
premade.summary: An abandoned amusement park where every ride has been rebuilt as a deathtrap.

premade.name: The Pit Superhuman Prison
premade.summary: A maximum-security prison sunk into a desert mesa, built to hold the worst the world has.

premade.name: Forward Operating Base
premade.summary: Blast walls, hangars and tents behind razor wire: a military base for superhuman operations.

premade.name: Commonwealth Hall
premade.summary: Modeled on the user's own team base sheet: a skyscraper that holds a city block inside, with a portal to a remote dimensional annex.

premade.name: Blackwood House
premade.summary: A rambling haunted mansion whose resident ghosts have agreed to guard the living who now share it.

premade.name: Royal Castle
premade.summary: Curtain walls, a moat and a keep that has never fallen, ruled from a hall of banners.

premade.name: Wizard's Spire
premade.summary: A crooked stone spire whose stairs climb far higher than the tower is tall.

premade.name: Dwarven Hold
premade.summary: Halls carved into the roots of a mountain, lit by forge-fire and guarded by rune-doors.

premade.name: Elven Treehold
premade.summary: Silver-barked platforms and bridges high in an ancient forest canopy.

premade.name: Thieves' Guild Warren
premade.summary: Cellars beneath the market linked by secret doors, trapped corridors and a counting-house vault.

premade.name: Temple of the Dawn
premade.summary: A white-marble temple whose dome lights up at sunrise, a sanctuary for the hurt and hunted.

premade.name: Dragon's Lair
premade.crew: One ancient dragon and kobold servants
premade.summary: A cavern in a volcanic peak where an ancient wyrm sleeps on a mountain of gold.

premade.name: Lich's Necropolis
premade.crew: A lich and its undead legion
premade.summary: A city of tombs beneath a dead marsh, where the lich has waited a thousand years.

premade.name: Pirate Cove
premade.summary: A sea cave hidden by a waterfall, with a hidden anchorage, a tavern and buried treasure.

premade.name: Floating Sky-Citadel
premade.summary: A walled city on a floating island, its waterfalls pouring into empty sky.

premade.name: Adventurers' Guildhall
premade.crew: A guildmaster, staff and wandering heroes
premade.summary: A rowdy timber hall with a job board, a training yard and rooms above the tavern.

premade.name: Druid's Grove
premade.summary: A ring of standing stones in a hidden valley where the old powers still answer.

premade.name: Mountain Monastery
premade.summary: A cliffside monastery above the clouds where martial disciplines are taught in silence.

premade.name: Witch's Cottage
premade.crew: A hedge witch and her familiar
premade.summary: A thatched cottage in the deep wood, roomier inside than it looks, smelling of herbs.
